In 1971, eight ordinary Americans did something extraordinary. They broke into an FBI office in Media, Pennsylvania, and stole government documents exposing a secret campaign against American citizens exercising their constitutional rights. Their actions helped expose what would become one of the most notorious domestic intelligence scandals in American history: COINTELPRO, the FBI's Counterintelligence Program. But exposing government wrongdoing and obtaining justice for its victims are two entirely different things. Somewhere in our forties or fifties, many of us start noticing changes. Energy dips earlier in the day. Sleep isn't as restful. Workouts take longer to recover from, the waistline creeps outward, and mood or libido may not be what it used to be. It's natural to wonder whether something specific is behind it, and whether there's a treatment that could help. Hormonal changes are one possible explanation, and hormone therapy is an option some adults explore. articles.title: The Strange Resurrection of Lonesome Dove
articles.author: Ross Barkan
articles.content_excerpt: On TikTok, there are dozens and dozens of videos of men and women, many of them young, staring into the camera to talk earnestly about an eight-hundred-page novel that was published forty-one years ago. “I didn’t see the western phase of my life coming, but I’m glad we’re here,” one woman says . “I want to talk about Lonesome Dove . . . . ” And this is what they do. They rhapsodize over characters who “feel like they are a part of your life.” They celebrate the “absolute journey” and the “incredible” prose. “I’ve tried to find a better book than Lonesome Dove and I’ve failed miserably, many times,” a twenty-year-old British man declares . articles.title: How Much Liberty Should We Limit?
articles.author: Sarah Conly
articles.content_excerpt: In the political culture of the United States, individual liberty is frequently thought of as possessing intrinsic and overriding importance. The political right and the political left in the United States have long competed to be seen as the true champions of individual freedom, and each has tried to advance its own goals under the banner of liberty. For the Right in recent decades, individual liberty has often meant the right of corporations and the wealthy to do whatever they want with their property, unconstrained by government regulation or obligations to pay taxes or collectively bargain with their workers.
